stem: In which example is it not possible for the underlined object to be in equilibrium?

options.A: An aeroplane climbs at a steady rate.
options.B: An aeroplane tows a glider at a constant altitude.
options.C: A speedboat changes direction at a constant speed.
options.D: Two boats tow a ship into harbour.

stem: Which single condition must apply for an object to be in equilibrium?

options.A: The object has a constant non-zero acceleration.
options.C: There are no forces acting on the object.
options.D: The resultant force acting on the object is zero.

stem:
A student states that:
‘If an object is in equilibrium, the sum of the clockwise moments about a point X is equal
to the sum of the anticlockwise moments about a point Y.’
Which condition would make the student’s statement correct?

options.A: Either X or Y is the centre of gravity of the object.
options.B: Either X or Y is the pivot of the object.
options.C: X and Y are at opposite ends of the object.
options.D: X and Y are the same point on the object.
